title: London rail network: six centrality measures and recorded removal sequences

degree.label: Degree
degree.short_definition: How many direct connections does a station have?
degree.definition: Number of incident connections divided by N-1 (400). Higher values identify stations with more immediate neighbours.

betweenness.label: Betweenness
betweenness.short_definition: How often do shortest paths pass through a station?
betweenness.definition: Normalised betweenness on the unweighted undirected graph. Shortest paths minimise the number of connections. Tied shortest paths share credit.

closeness.label: Closeness
closeness.short_definition: How few connections separate a station from the rest?
closeness.definition: NetworkX closeness on the initially connected unweighted graph: (N-1) divided by the sum of shortest-path distances in connections to all other stations.

weighted_degree.label: Flow-weighted degree
weighted_degree.unit: sum of incident AM-peak edge flows
weighted_degree.short_definition: How much recorded edge flow meets at a station?
weighted_degree.definition: Sum of the supplied passenger-flow weights on incident connections. This is not a count of unique passengers entering or using the station.

weighted_betweenness.label: Inverse-flow betweenness
weighted_betweenness.short_definition: Which stations bridge routes when high-flow links count as stronger?
weighted_betweenness.definition: Normalised betweenness using 1/flow as connection cost. High-flow connections have smaller cost. This is not an assignment of actual passenger routes.

weighted_closeness.label: Length-weighted closeness
weighted_closeness.short_definition: Which stations have the shortest physical network distances?
weighted_closeness.definition: NetworkX closeness using connection length in metres. This measures physical network proximity, not passenger volume or journey time.

provenance.method: Deterministic reproduction of notebook cells4 and18 from original GraphML. No notebook execution or calibration. Connected components recomputed only for the original saved removal sequences.
display_notes: Coordinates rounded to0.001metres; measure values rounded to14decimal places.
Size or colour should be normalised within a chosen measure. Equal visual emphasis across maps does not mean equal numerical units or magnitudes.
The 401-station supplied graph includes Underground, Overground and DLR links; it is not the complete current system.
Incident edge-flow totals are not unique passenger counts. Inverse-flow shortest paths are not observed passenger itineraries.
Removal states reproduce graph connectivity, not service operation, disruption probabilities, rerouting or congestion.
Colouring all nodes outside the largest component as disconnected means disconnected from that component only; they may remain connected to each other.
Stations are removed without replacement edges. A real station closure can have different operational semantics, such as trains passing through without stopping.
